result.title: ANCHOR: Audio-Visually Grounded Chain-of-Thought Reasoning Benchmark
result.comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026, Evaluations & Datasets Track. Joel Julin and Souraja Kundu are co-first authors
result.summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) perform well on audio-visual question answering, but correct answers do not necessarily imply that their stated reasoning is grounded in relevant perceptual evidence. Existing benchmarks mainly evaluate final-answer accuracy, offering limited insight into whether model-generated rationales correctly identify visual regions, temporal intervals, and audio events supporting predictions. We introduce ANCHOR, a benchmark and evaluation framework for measuring grounded-rationale alignment in multimodal reasoning, comprising 2,319 videos and 8,272 question-answer pairs with structured reasoning traces, temporal evidence, spatial bounding boxes, and salient audio cues, including a human-refined test set of 224 videos and 975 question-answer pairs. We separately measure answer correctness, hallucination, logical divergence, and conciseness, with direct spatial and temporal grounding measurements on a focused subset. Across the full benchmark, twelve contemporary MLLMs show a substantial alignment gap: models with comparable answer performance can differ markedly in whether their explanations are supported by annotated evidence. On a matched subset of 100 videos and 446 question-answer pairs, rankings remain highly stable across human-refined, Gemini-generated, and GPT-generated references (mean Pearson r=0.99), providing evidence against model-reference circularity within this subset. Grounding-cue ablations of three MLLMs on the full human-refined test set reveal a consistent modality hierarchy: removing video reduces accuracy by 38.4-41.8 points, while removing bounding boxes (3.2-7.7 points) and audio (4.2-5.6 points) causes smaller, complementary, model-dependent drops. These findings show answer-only evaluation obscures important grounding failures and position ANCHOR as a testbed for evaluating accurate and evidence-aligned audio-visual reasoning.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 ANCHOR 音视频 grounded chain-of-thought 推理基准与评测框架，含 2,319 段视频、8,272 个 QA 对及结构化推理链、时序证据、空间框和音频线索，分别测量答案正确性、幻觉、逻辑偏离、简洁性与空间/时序 grounding，并对多种 grounding 线索做消融。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接针对「推理链是否真正基于感知证据」而非仅答案正确，与 LVR 关注的答案是否使用视觉内容、视觉旁路与证据筛选相关；其移除视频/框/音频的消融可为核查视觉证据的因果贡献提供线索，但对象是文本 CoT 而非 latent 状态，需人工核查其与内部表示的对应。
